clue.text: This person clutching short order for something from pharmacy

indicators.note: one piece holds another inside it, as a hand clutches something

parts.note: this person's, belonging to the speaker, is MINE

indicators.note: short means the word is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: an edict is an official order

explanation.surface: Someone holding a brief prescription while waiting for an item from the chemist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'This person' stands for the possessive 'this person's', a stretch the solver must allow; 'short' drops the final letter of the order.
explanation.definitionFit: Medicine is the typical product dispensed by a pharmacy or chemist's shop.

clue.text: With the knot tied, not one to be spoiled

indicators.note: not means without, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: to tie the knot is to get married
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Marriage, minus a single person, seen as something ruined.
explanation.definitionFit: Marred means damaged or spoilt in appearance or quality.

clue.text: Little lady with oomph is no credit

parts.note: deb is short for debutante, a young society lady
it means sex appeal, as in the it girl

explanation.surface: A young woman with sex appeal is not to her credit.
explanation.definitionFit: In accounting a debit is the opposite of a credit.

clue.text: Perfect little rug — use outside

indicators.note: one word goes around the other

parts.note: to consume is to use up
a mat is a small rug

explanation.surface: An ideal small rug — use it outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Consummate as an adjective means complete, perfect, supremely skilled.

clue.text: Sin? Last thing to be associated with the bishop!

indicators.note: the last thing belonging to the next word is its final letter

parts.note: RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: Sin being the last thing a bishop should be linked with.
explanation.definitionFit: To err is to do wrong or to sin.

clue.text: Little person, not half unhappy type?

parts.note: wee is Scottish and informal for little

indicators.note: keeping only half the word, the first three of its six letters

explanation.surface: Asking whether a small person is only partly a miserable sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' keeps the first half of PERSON, giving PER.
explanation.definitionFit: A weeper is someone who cries, an unhappy sort of person.

clue.text: Having got rid of cold, stop and relax

indicators.note: getting rid of means a letter is removed

parts.note: cease means stop
C is cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Once your cold is gone, stop and take it easy.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off means to slacken or relax.

clue.text: At the bottom of empty pool a sticky substance is setting

indicators.note: in a down entry the later pieces sit below the first
emptying a word removes its insides, leaving the outer letters

parts.note: cement is an adhesive binding substance

explanation.surface: Cement left at the bottom of a drained pool is setting hard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' leaves PL from pool; 'At the bottom of' puts A and CEMENT below it in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A placement or setting is the position where something is put.

clue.text: Ornamental container woman's taken to loft

parts.note: Rose is a woman's name
to loft a ball is to send it high, as a bowler might

explanation.surface: A decorative vessel that a woman has carried up to the attic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loft' looks like an attic; here it is a verb, to send a ball upwards, like bowl.
explanation.definitionFit: A rose bowl is a decorative bowl for displaying flowers, often given as a trophy.

clue.text: Bird beginning to roost on old rubbish receptacle

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: a bin is a container for rubbish

explanation.surface: A bird settling down to roost on top of an old dustbin.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin is a common small songbird with a red breast.

clue.text: Old people, quiet folk in Moscow maybe

parts.note: P, piano, is the musical direction for quiet
people living in Moscow are, for example, Russians

explanation.surface: Elderly, softly spoken people who might be living in Moscow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old people' looks like pensioners; it means a nation of the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Prussia was a German kingdom and state that no longer exists, so its inhabitants are a historical people.

clue.text: Greek character, see, with gift — given to the female who seeks wisdom?

parts.note: phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
lo is an old word meaning look or see
a sop is a small gift to placate someone
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A Greek figure gives a present to a woman searching for wisdom.
explanation.definitionFit: The word's Greek root means lover of wisdom, so a thinker is one who seeks it.

clue.text: Discontented, being not fully paid

definitions.meaning: a debt not settled in full is not discharged

explanation.surface: Unhappy because one's wages were not paid in full.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both displeased and, of a debt, not settled.

clue.text: False Messiah, nut showing zeal

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so these letters are rearranged into a new word

explanation.surface: A fake messiah, a crank, displaying fervour.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeal and the answer are synonyms for eager, passionate devotion.

clue.text: Auntie seen on reflection not to have changed

indicators.text: seen on reflection not to have changed
indicators.note: reading the word backwards, as in a mirror, leaves it exactly the same

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: An aunt who, when looked at again, has not changed at all.
explanation.walkthrough: Auntie and the Beeb are both British nicknames for the BBC; the answer reads the same either way.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are affectionate British nicknames for the BBC broadcaster.

clue.text: Get rid of nasty boil — treat with calamine finally

indicators.note: nasty suggests something messed up, so the letters are rearranged
finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Getting rid of an unpleasant boil by dabbing on calamine at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nasty' turns BOIL and TREAT into OBLITERAT; 'finally' adds E from calamine.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate something is to destroy or wipe it out completely.

clue.text: Search endlessly for item of furniture nice to sit in

indicators.note: without its end, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: to comb an area is to search it thoroughly
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Hunting at length for a piece of furniture that is pleasant to sit in.
explanation.definitionFit: Something comfortable, such as a chair, is pleasant and easy to sit in.

clue.text: Outside a capital city study a type of ornamentation

indicators.note: one word placed around the others

parts.note: to con is to study carefully
Paris is the capital of France

explanation.surface: Studying a style of decoration on the edge of a capital.
explanation.definitionFit: A caparison is an ornamental cloth covering for a horse, a decorative trapping.

clue.text: Nasty smell associated with a snake

parts.note: BO is body odour

explanation.surface: A bad smell linked to a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: The boa is a large constricting serpent.

clue.text: Goose in farm building, one that's left trapped

parts.note: a barn is a farm building

indicators.note: one piece is caught inside another

parts.note: an ace is a one in cards
L is left

explanation.surface: A goose in a barn, with one bird left shut in.
explanation.definitionFit: The barnacle goose is a black-and-white Arctic species of wild goose.

clue.text: Nothing left after home's been gone over

indicators.note: the left piece is placed after the other
gone over means turned over, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: Nothing remained after the house had been searched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'home's' is read as 'home has'; 'been gone over' means turned over, and 'after' places the left abbreviation behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Nil is zero, especially in a sports score.

clue.text: Son messing with art covered in dye — George is that?

indicators.note: one piece wrapped around another, which sits covered inside it

parts.note: paint and dye both colour a surface

indicators.note: messing with means jumbling, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A son making a mess of artwork and ending up covered in dye.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks George as one example: he is England's patron saint. 'messing with' jumbles the five letters; 'covered in' wraps the dye round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint George is the patron saint of England, the protector chosen for the nation.

clue.text: Media story must avoid all extremes — I'll see to that?

indicators.note: both words lose their first and last letters

explanation.surface: A news story must not be extreme, says the one in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper's editor oversees and checks every story printed.

clue.text: Refusal by jolly folk is what you'd expect

parts.note: no is a refusal
a Jolly is slang for a Royal Marine; RM is Royal Marines

explanation.surface: A refusal from cheerful people is only to be expected.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jolly' is old naval slang for a Royal Marine, abbreviated RM.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is the usual standard, what is typical or expected.

clue.text: I have two lines in small part as an old man?

indicators.note: the pieces go inside another word

parts.note: a shred is a small fragment
I have contracts to I've
L is line, so two lines are LL

explanation.surface: An actor with only a couple of lines in a bit part, playing an old man.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a minor stage role; 'in' signals the insertion. The definition is a whimsical description of how age leaves a man.
explanation.definitionFit: Old age can leave a man wrinkled and withered, so he looks shrunken.

clue.text: Quick-moving match?

definitions.meaning: something used to give a flame

explanation.surface: A fast-paced game.
explanation.definitionFit: Light means agile, and a light is something to ignite a cigarette, such as a match.

clue.text: Wagon is secure with article locked inside

indicators.note: one piece is placed within another

parts.note: to win something is to secure it
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A wagon kept safe with goods locked up inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A wain is an old word for a farm wagon or cart.

clue.text: Was one of the top performers about to bite into apple?

definitions.text: Was one of the top performers

indicators.note: a piece biting into another goes inside it

parts.note: a costard is an old English variety of cooking apple
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Asking whether a leading actor was about to take a bite of an apple.
explanation.walkthrough: A costard is a large English apple variety; RE goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To co-star is to share top billing with another lead actor.

clue.text: This food is in bar for one who can't pay his way

indicators.note: the food sits inside the word bar, so removing bar's letters leaves it

parts.words: one who can't pay his way
parts.note: a beggar cannot support himself
taken as written

explanation.surface: Pub food for a customer who cannot pay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' works backwards: the food placed inside the drinks counter's word spells the penniless person, so removing that word leaves the food.
explanation.definitionFit: An egg is a basic food, laid by hens.

clue.text: Gangster's inner apprehension

indicators.note: the answer lies within the letters of this word

explanation.surface: A gangster's private anxiety.
explanation.definitionFit: Angst is a feeling of deep anxiety or dread.

clue.text: Climatic effect has impacted on Nile

indicators.note: impacted suggests something knocked out of shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A weather phenomenon has affected the River Nile.
explanation.definitionFit: This Pacific warming event disrupts weather patterns around the world.

clue.text: Better teams possibly in Germany? Not a lot

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go inside the other piece
not a lot means without many, so those letters are removed

parts.note: many means a lot

indicators.note: possibly signals another arrangement of these letters

explanation.surface: Wondering whether stronger football teams are found in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Better' reads as an adjective; it is one who bets. 'Not a lot' removes a word for many, leaving GER; 'possibly' rearranges the teams into AMEST, which goes 'in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamester is a gambler, someone who places bets.
